title: uint32_t millis near the wrap. Only 100 ms passed. What does this print?
explain: start + 1000 wraps around to 704. Now now (4294967100) is bigger than 704, so it prints timeout after only 100 ms. Compare time with a subtraction: now - start > 1000. It stays right across the wrap.

title: Night light: on below 300, off above 400. Readings 350, 290, 350, 410, 350. What is printed?
explain: Between 300 and 400 the state does not change. 350: off. 290: on. 350: stays on. 410: off. 350: stays off. So you get 01100. One threshold would flicker around 350.

title: STM32 PA5 (pin 5). You turn the LED on and off with BSRR. What are the two values?
explain: BSRR low 16 bits set a pin. High 16 bits reset it. So set is 1 << 5 = 0x20 and reset is 1 << 21 = 0x200000. Writing 0 bits does nothing. This is one write, not read-modify-write, so an ISR cannot break it like it can with ODR.

title: a = 200, b = 100, both uint8_t. What does this print?
explain: In a + b both values are promoted to int, so the sum is 300 and 300 > 255 is true (1). Storing it back into a uint8_t keeps only 8 bits: 300 - 256 = 44. The wrap happens at the store, not in the addition.

title: Three 330 Ω resistors in parallel. What does the multimeter show (power off)?
explain: In parallel, 1/R = 1/330 + 1/330 + 1/330 = 3/330. So R = 330 / 3 = 110 Ω. Equal resistors in parallel: divide by the count. The total is always smaller than the smallest one.

title: Your 9 V divider: R1 = 10 kΩ, R2 = 4.7 kΩ, nothing connected to the output. How much current flows from the battery?
explain: The two resistors are in series: 10 k + 4.7 k = 14.7 kΩ. I = 9 V / 14700 Ω = 0.61 mA. A divider always burns this current. Bigger resistors waste less, but then a load or the ADC input changes the output more.

title: analogWrite(9, 191) on a 5 V Uno. A multimeter in DC volts is on pin 9. What does it show?
explain: 191 / 255 is about 75% duty. The pin is HIGH (5 V) for 75% of the time, LOW for 25%. The multimeter is slow and shows the average: 0.75 * 5 V = about 3.7 V.

title: The LED lights for 2 s after a press. During that time button presses are ignored. Tap the bug.
explain: delay(2000) blocks the whole loop(), so nothing else runs for 2 s. Add a LED_ON state, remember the start time with millis(), and check the time on every pass.

title: ISR does events++. loop() runs process() when events >= 10, then sets events = 0. What can go wrong?
options: Events that arrive during process() are lost
The ISR cannot write a volatile variable
explain: volatile only stops the compiler from caching the value. It does not make the code atomic. An event that arrives during process() is thrown away by events = 0. Also, on an 8-bit AVR, events -= 10 in loop() is a read-modify-write that the ISR can interrupt. Copy and subtract with interrupts off.

title: static int n; inside a function. First call does return ++n. Your Reset_Handler clears .bss. Where is n and what is returned?
explain: A static variable without an initial value goes to .bss. Your Reset_Handler zeroes .bss before main(), so the first call returns 1. If you skip the .bss clear, n starts with random RAM content.
